title: Calibration job orchestration: runs, artifacts, retention, and RBAC
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Scope: define and ship orchestration primitives in Redwood Console for calibration job runs and their resulting artifacts (quantization profiles, histograms, validation reports). This ticket covers: run lifecycle (create, run, retry, cancel, resume), artifact ingestion and immutable storage, retention policies (org/project defaults + overrides), permission model (who can start runs, who can view/download artifacts, who can request extended retention), UI surfaces (Runs list, Run detail, Artifacts tab), and API + webhook endpoints for automation. Accuracy validation: include baseline comparison, automated pass/fail based on eval thresholds, and a manual QA approval step for releasing a profile to Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console UI: users can create a calibration job (select model, quantization target FP8/INT8, calibration dataset, eval set, and thresholds).
2) Runs API: POST /v1/projects/{p}/calibration_runs creates a run and returns run_id; run status transitions (pending -> running -> succeeded|failed|cancelled) visible via GET.
3) Artifacts: calibration profile, per-layer histograms, and validation report are stored under a project-scoped artifact namespace and are immutable once the run is marked succeeded.
4) Retention: project-level default retention applied; owners can request longer retention via a retention exception flow. Artifacts older than TTL are deleted and deletions recorded in audit logs.
5) RBAC: role-based rules enforced: "calibration.run" to start runs, "calibration.view" to see run metadata and artifacts, "calibration.export" to download artifacts. Admins can grant/ revoke at org/project scope.
6) Accuracy gating: runs automatically compute evaluation metrics and mark runs as passed/failed against configured thresholds; failing runs are flagged in UI and notify owners.
7) Integration: artifacts uploaded to configured storage (S3/GCS) with server-side encryption and KMS key attribution; console shows artifact URLs and an API to fetch signed download links.
8) Audit & notifications: all run lifecycle events generate audit log entries and configurable webhooks for external CI/automation.
updates: 2026-02-25: Ticket created after product review — converged on scope to include retention exceptions and RBAC mapping.
2026-02-28: Design sketch uploaded to Confluence (link below). Decided to keep artifacts immutable once run succeeded to avoid drift and ensure traceability.

2026-03-02: Security review kickoff — potential data leakage vector identified for artifacts containing model inputs; security requested artifact sanitization and opt-in plaintext capture for compliance customers.

2026-03-05: Implementation approach drafted with ENG: storage adapter abstraction (S3/GCS), artifact metadata catalog in Console DB, and a background garbage-collector job for TTL enforcement. Planning to split work: ENG-runtime (calibration runner) + ENG-console (UI/API) + ENG-platform (storage + KMS + audit).
risks: storage-costs if project teams request long default retention for large numbers of runs and per-layer histograms
artifact contents may include sensitive prompt inputs — need sanitization or explicit opt-in for capturing raw inputs
RBAC model complexity when mapping existing org roles to calibration-specific privileges
next_steps: Product sign-off on acceptance criteria and RBAC matrix (owners: Security, Platform, Console PM)
ENG to produce implementation plan and break into sprint-sized tickets (runtime + console + platform)
Create E2E smoke test plan using a small OpenEncoder model and a canonical eval set to validate accuracy gating and retention cleanup
